title: Group and ungroup what you selected
goal: Select a box and its label, press Command G, and they become one thing you can move, hide, lock and delete together. Shift Command G takes it apart again and leaves the pieces exactly where they were.
notes:
Flag: next-layer-groups, Next only, on by default. Photoshop parity on the keys: Command G groups, Shift Command G ungroups. EditorCommands.swift holds the menu command groups; EditorState.swift owns the selection set and every mutation goes through History.perform. Canvas selection, marquee and drag live in CanvasView.swift, which is already large, so put the group specific canvas logic in its own file the way the measure work did with CanvasMeasure.swift. Depends on the group model and the group renderer.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). The first rung of the component ladder a person actually sees.
acceptance: The Layer menu gains Group with Command G and Ungroup with Shift Command G, each enabled only when the selection allows it
Clicking a group on the canvas selects the whole group and dragging it moves everything inside; double clicking goes inside so one piece can be picked
Grouping, ungrouping, moving and deleting a group each undo in one step

Try it: open Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next, flag next-layer-groups on, draw a rectangle and a text layer, select both, press Command G, drag the group, press Shift Command G, press Command Z twice
Resizing a group is out of this slice and is filed as a follow-up task, with what should happen to the pieces inside written down
Audit written under queue/audits/, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The layers list is a SEPARATE task, so right after Command G the pieces vanish from a flat list and one row named Group appears. Confusing but bounded, and it is the very next task; the audit says so. Numbered names (Group, Group 2) so two groups are tellable apart. (2) Resize handles and the rotate knob must be SUPPRESSED on a group, not left drawing: a group's stored size is unused, so dragging a handle would look like it did nothing while burning an undo step. Resizing a group is out of this slice by the task itself and is filed as a follow-up. (3) The app reads layer.frame everywhere as if it were canvas space. That is true for a top-level layer and WRONG for a child inside a group, so the moment double click descends, the selection outline, the caption pill, measure handles and the rotate knob would all draw at the wrong place. The fix is one boundary rather than dozens of call sites: the canvas asks for canvas-space layers and commits canvas-space frames, and EditorState converts once on the way in and out. The Position and Size fields keep showing PARENT space, which is what the spec asks for. (4) Escape has to step out of a group BEFORE it clears the selection, slotted into the priority ladder the canvas already runs. (5) Double click on a text layer opens it for typing today, and that check runs before anything else; descending has to win when the hit is deeper than where you are, or a group holding a label could never be entered. (6) A marquee on empty canvas resets you to the top level, so there is always one obvious way out. (7) Shortest version: no group resize, no group rotate, no group styling UI, no drag between groups on canvas, no enter-group visual chrome beyond the selection outline.

Built. Core: canGroup / canUngroup / ungroupLayers (all the selected groups in one mutation), freshGroupName, and the click walk — selectionTarget picks the outermost thing you are not already inside, descendTarget goes one level deeper. The change that made the rest possible: canvasLayer(id:) hands back a layer with its frame on the canvas, CanvasView reads that everywhere it used to read layer.frame, and EditorState.previewCanvasFrame / commitCanvasFrame convert back into the space a layer is stored in (a group translating through moveLayer(id:toCanvasOrigin:), since a group's frame is an anchor and not a box). Without that boundary, the moment a double click reached a piece inside a group its outline, handles, caption pill and measure dots would all have drawn one group offset away. App: flag next-layer-groups (Next, on by default), Layer menu Group ⌘G and Ungroup ⇧⌘G above the arrange commands and absent when the flag is off, groupContextID in EditorState with Escape stepping out one level, and CanvasGroups.swift holding the canvas side. Position and Size keeps showing PARENT space, per the spec.

Second review, on the built app. (1) Descending had no sign of itself: the handles moved to one piece and nothing else changed, so a group you are inside now draws its own faint dotted box, quarter-strength selection blue, finely dotted so it does not compete with the selection outline. (2) A group draws no resize handles and no rotate knob, and W and H are greyed behind a plain sentence saying a group is as big as what is inside it, rather than the arrow tool's "drag this shape's ends" copy. (3) Still rough and filed: the Layers list is flat, so a group is one row and NO row highlights while you are inside one (that is the next task); a group cannot be resized (resize-a-group-and-the-pieces-inside-follow, which has to write the scaling rule down first because the design doc currently promises groups never scale); the only canvas route to a multi-selection is a marquee sweep (shift-click-on-the-canvas-adds-a-layer-to-the-se).

Acceptance checked on the probe with a new 50-step walk, Scripts/playtest/group-walk.json. (1) The menu dump reads "Group ⌘G" and "Ungroup ⇧⌘G" in the Layer menu above Bring to Front; both are disabled without a selection that allows them (canGroupSelection needs two unlocked layers of one list, canUngroupSelection an unlocked group). (2) A marquee over a rectangle and a text layer then ⌘G leaves 2 layers and one selection box around both; dragging from (500,400) to (620,300) moved the group and the ungrouped rectangle later read frame (360,140), exactly the drag delta from (240,240), with the text carried along; a double click selected the rectangle alone (X 0 Y 0 W 660 H 400, parent space) and Escape re-selected the group. (3) Undo: ⇧⌘G then three undos walk back one step each — group restored still dragged, drag undone, group undone with the rectangle back at (240,240). (4) The try-it walk is in the audit. (5) Resize filed as resize-a-group-and-the-pieces-inside-follow with the scaling question written into it. (6) Audit queue/audits/2026-09-03-group-and-ungroup.json with three real window captures; rough items filed. Scripts/test.sh green at 1630, 31 new tests.
